explanation: Two-part retrospective detector. (1) Context-robust triggers fire at about 0.3-1.0 of max in any register: a number word straight after a determiner ('the two', 'the three', 'these two', ~0.45-0.7; bare 'two' after a verb only ~0.2-0.3), the last suffix subword of a word the tokenizer splits (Efferves|cent, Fires|ide, pharmac|ist, prot|racted, unwield|y, ~0.45-1.0), and 'about' in 'brought about' (~0.3-0.45). (2) Register-gated triggers fire at about 0.3-0.8 only in first/second-person, dialogue-like or dummy-subject clauses: object/addressee 'you'/'us'/'your' ('gave you', 'send you', 'thank you', 'Can you'), 'one'/'more' after 'have', 'some', 'one', 'anything', 'don't have', and the copula after 'It', 'There' or 'I' ('It was', 'There is', 'I am'). The same register-gated words stay below ~0.2 in third-person descriptive or news prose whose subject is a full noun phrase ('The company hired more workers', 'The river has more water', 'The soldiers marched past you', 'Rain was'), as do 'him'/'them' after 'send' and ordinary narrative with no such tokens.
